sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 2.2, second paragraph, p.5 of the published version (arXiv v2 Lemma 2.2, p.6)
sourceIssues.correction: m should be the Cartier index of K_X + S at P, the log index. For the plt surface germ obtained by localising at P, this equals the order of the local class group, and the conclusions then hold.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample. Take X = Spec k[x,y,z]/(xy − z²), the A1 surface singularity with char k > 5, S = V(x, z), Δ = S and P the vertex. Then X is Q-factorial, (X, S) is plt and hence dlt, and P is a codimension-one point of the curve S. The minimal resolution (charts (x,z,y) = (u,uv,uv²) and (st²,st,s)) is crepant, so K_X is Cartier and m = 1. But div(x) = 2S and the ideal (x, z) is not principal at P, so S is not Cartier. Since f*S = S′ + E/2, adjunction gives (K_X + S)|_S = K_S + ½P, not K_S. With m = index(K_X + S) = 2 every clause holds. For a threefold example, multiply by A¹. The only other use is Lemma 4.2 (p.16), which needs only that the different of a plt pair with standard coefficients has standard coefficients; that is unaffected. Checked on the page image. Noted by the extraction (gap-index, item adjunction-index-diagnostic).

sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 2.16, p.13 of the published version (arXiv v2 Lemma 2.16, p.14)
sourceIssues.correction: Also fix a finite set I ⊂ [0, 1) and require the coefficients of B to lie in I. Then, over the minimal resolution, the exceptional discrepancies take finitely many values. This is what the proof of Proposition 2.15 needs, since the boundaries B_n of a flip sequence all have the coefficients of B.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample. On the A1 surface S = {xy = z²} with C = V(x, z) and B = bC, 0 < b < 1/2, the minimal resolution is one (−2)-curve E, and K_{S′} + bC′ + (b/2)E = f*(K_S + bC). The pair is ½-lc for every such b (log discrepancies 1 − b/2 and 1 − b on an snc model with coefficients < 1/2), and there is one exceptional discrepancy, −b/2, so m = 1. That value varies infinitely. The proof fails because the right-hand sides B_{S′}·C_i of its linear system contain f^{-1}_*B·C_i, which varies with B. With coefficients in I the right-hand sides lie in a finite set, since f^{-1}_*B·C_i = 2r_i + a_iC_i² − Σ_{j≠i}(1 − a_j)C_j·C_i < 2r_i ≤ 8. Proposition 2.15 is unaffected. Noted by the extraction (gap-surface, item surface-finiteness-diagnostic); the corrected statement is proved in fixed-boundary-surface by this continuation.

sourceIssues.correction: Retain a neighborhood of the special fibre in the local deformation lemma; add properness for its global application. The unrestricted global statements fail.
sourceIssues.reason: For R=Z_p, p>5, remove only the closed special vertex from Spec R[x,y,z,w]/(xy−zw). This is an integral flat normal excellent scheme with smooth special fibre. The closed remaining generic vertex Z is disjoint from that fibre. The ruling D=V(x,z) is Cartier away from Z and restricts to a Cartier divisor on the smooth special fibre, but it is not Q-Cartier at the generic node. On the explicit small resolution xt=zs,wt=ys, its strict-transform divisor line bundle has degree−1 on the exceptional P¹. A Cartier multiple would pull back trivially on that fibre, contradicting degree−m. The report provides the charts. Properness repairs globalization by the closed-image argument, conditional on the local theorem. (cc-442dc5) Rechecked in arXiv v2 (there Lemma 6.4): the proof is only a citation of [KM92, 12.1.8] and [dFH11, Proposition 3.1], which are local statements near the special fibre, so the unrestricted global formulation is not supported by its proof either.
